intro: Health is an ever-present exam topic: making a doctor's appointment, symptoms, a chat at the pharmacy. Special attention: the «Rozmowa» with a doctor and a letter to a friend with advice.
speaking.0.promptUa: Describe the illustration. Say where these people are, what they are doing and how they feel. Also say what you think the doctor will do.
speaking.0.phrases.0.ua: In the illustration I can see a clinic.
speaking.0.phrases.2.ua: Probably he has a cold or the flu.
speaking.0.phrases.3.ua: The doctor will examine him and prescribe medicine.
speaking.0.tips.0: Useful for health topics: «wygląda na + accusative»: «wygląda na chorego / zmęczonego».
speaking.0.tips.1: Don't know the name of the illness — say «ma objawy przeziębienia» (has cold symptoms).
speaking.0.tips.2: Finish with a prediction: «za chwilę…», «prawdopodobnie…» — the «co dalej» point requires it.
speaking.1.promptUa: Tell us what you do to look after your health. Explain what is hardest for you and what you would like to change.
speaking.1.phrases.0.ua: I try to look after my health.
speaking.1.phrases.1.ua: The hardest thing for me is…
speaking.1.phrases.2.ua: Next month I want to start…
speaking.1.tips.0: **Staram się + infinitive** («I try to») — politely admits imperfection and sounds natural.
speaking.1.tips.1: An example from your own life brings the monologue alive: numbers («dwa razy w tygodniu»), frequency, time.
speaking.1.tips.2: Advice at the end («radzę wszystkim…») is a good, natural conclusion.
speaking.2.promptUa: You are at a family doctor's appointment. Describe your symptoms, answer the doctor's questions and ask about a sick note.
speaking.2.phrases.0.ua: My throat has been sore for three days.
speaking.2.phrases.2.ua: Can I get a sick note?
speaking.2.phrases.3.ua: What should I do to get better faster?
speaking.2.tips.0: **Boli mnie + nominative** — «my head hurts» in Polish is «boli mnie głowa»: the body part is the subject here.
speaking.2.tips.1: Say numbers and doses clearly: «trzy razy dziennie po jedzeniu».
speaking.2.tips.2: Didn't understand — ask again: «Przepraszam, czy mógłby Pan powiedzieć to jeszcze raz wolniej?»
writing.0.promptUa: On Friday you have a dentist's appointment but you must cancel it. Write a short message to the clinic: apologise, give the reason and suggest a new date.
writing.0.phrases.0.ua: Unfortunately I have to cancel the appointment.
writing.0.phrases.1.ua: I'm very sorry for the trouble.
writing.0.phrases.2.ua: Could I make an appointment for…?
writing.0.tips.0: A formal short note: **greeting → who → problem → reason → request → thanks**.
writing.0.tips.1: **Bardzo przepraszam za kłopot** — a universal polite formula for cancellations and rescheduling.
writing.1.promptUa: Your friend wrote that she has been tired for a week and often has a headache. Write her a letter: express concern, tell her about a similar experience of your own, give three pieces of advice and suggest meeting.
writing.1.phrases.0.ua: I'm very worried after your letter.
writing.1.phrases.1.ua: I once had a similar problem.
writing.1.phrases.2.ua: I advise you to… / You should…
writing.1.tips.0: In an informal letter **Ty/Ci/Cię/Twój** are capitalised — it's the letter-writing convention.
writing.1.tips.1: It's better to number the three pieces of advice in words: **po pierwsze / po drugie / po trzecie** — the structure is visible at once.
writing.1.tips.2: A complex sentence with **żeby** («umów się, żeby sprawdzić…») is a small step towards B2.
listening.0.intro: Listen to the phone conversation and choose the correct answers.
grammar.0.intro: Choose the correct form. Topic: health, doctor, medicine.
grammar.0.questions.0.why: The accusative of inanimate masculine nouns = the nominative: «przepisał antybiotyk».
grammar.0.questions.1.why: The action is still going on → present tense: «od tygodnia czuję się źle» (as in Ukrainian «вже тиждень почуваюся»).
